The description contains conditional or minimizing statements that fail the strict no-negative-signal criterion:
- "Apply it over gel polish or regular polish (with a compatible top coat)": a conditional requirement for regular polish use.
- "For the full effect, use a glossy top coat": implies the product falls short without it. This addresses the reviewer complaint "Don't forget to buy a gloss top coat!!!" in a defensive way.
- "Thin layers and gentle buffing create the smoothest finish": implies a less smooth result otherwise, i.e., a care condition.
- "A little goes a long way, so one jar can cover many manicures": minimizes the "Not much product for the money at all" complaint, which the criterion counts as negative when the same issue is addressed.
- "Because this powder is dense, a small amount covers an entire nail": reframes the reviewers' concern about the small quantity of powder in the jar, a minimizing reassurance.
Per the instruction to lean toward failing when unsure, this fails.
